intentionalExceptions: The NVIDIA profile pins onnxruntime-gpu to the CUDA 12 line (1.26.x) because ONNX Runtime 1.27+ ships a CUDA-13-only default GPU wheel; the CPU profile is free to track the newer 1.28 CPU fixes, and CUDA 13 is reported as a separate untested manual lane (see backend.dependency_caps.PROVIDER_LANES).

Python 3.10 is no longer a supported setup target because the security-reviewed ONNX Runtime 1.25+ CPU/CUDA line and the pinned DirectML 1.24.4 line do not publish CPython 3.10 wheels; Python 3.11 is the minimum reproducible runtime.

2026-08-12: NumPy is pinned to 2.4.6, the newest 2.4.x release that supports Python 3.11; NumPy 2.5.x starts at Python 3.12, so the >=3.11 project floor is intentionally retained until a coordinated Python-floor review.

2026-08-12: CPU and DirectML profiles advance to torch==2.13.0/torchvision==0.28.0; NVIDIA advances to torch==2.11.0/torchvision==0.26.0 because the existing CUDA 12.8 PyTorch index exposes 2.11.0 as its newest compatible wheel. Do not move NVIDIA to the CUDA 13 channel without a coordinated ONNX Runtime CUDA-lane review.

PaddleOCR, EasyOCR, and simple-lama remain reviewed opt-ins rather than default setup packages because their OpenCV wheel ownership or NumPy caps conflict with the primary OpenCV 5 and NumPy 2 runtime.

Native wheel hashes are not embedded in pip constraints because the supported Python, Windows, Linux, CPU, CUDA, and DirectML matrix produces different artifacts; exact versions, profile hashes, the frozen SBOM, and pip-audit evidence remain mandatory.
PyTorch and PaddlePaddle use vendor indexes whose platform-specific wheels are resolved during setup; release evidence records the reviewed index list and resolved artifact versions.
The Docker image installs the CPU profile's core smoke subset rather than optional OCR and PyTorch backends; it is a local pipeline smoke image, not the frozen Windows distribution.
